My conversations with Matrix General Contractor (MGC) owner Andrey Tapias Espana began in February, when he assured me he would be able to replace my roof. I signed my first contract with MGC in March. There was a lengthy back-and-forth process between MGC and my homeowners insurance company to get the roof approved and covered. Once everything was finalized, I signed a second contract for the remaining work, expecting the project to move forward.

Unfortunately, my experience since then has been extremely disappointing.

Andrey confirmed he would begin work on July 20, but he never showed up and never called. I had to repeatedly call and text him before I finally received a response saying he would not be coming that day. My sister had taken time off work to stay at my house for the scheduled appointment, and that time was completely wasted.

He then rescheduled for July 23. I had another sibling wait at my home, but once again, no one arrived. After repeatedly assuring me he was on his way, Andrey finally showed up after 3:00 p.m.—alone, with no crew or materials. Instead of starting the roof, he explained that he was dealing with personal matters and promised that work would definitely begin on July 29 at 8:00 a.m.

To avoid another scheduling issue, I had Andrey text me the July 29 date and time and asked him to save it in his phone. I stayed home on July 29 waiting, but once again, he never showed. He later claimed that he somehow had me scheduled for July 30 instead.

Today is July 30. This morning, Andrey texted me saying his employees would arrive between 8:00 and 9:00 a.m. That time changed to 10:00 a.m., then 11:00 a.m. Eventually, his employee, Santos, called me and said they would not be coming today after all and asked if they could come on Saturday. At that point, I told him absolutely not and called Andrey to request a full refund of my funds.

Shortly after, Andrey called Santos and then called me back, saying they would actually be at my house today at 3:00 p.m. to begin the work.

At this point, after months of waiting and multiple missed appointments, broken promises, poor communication, and having my family repeatedly rearrange their schedules for no-shows, I have lost confidence in this company. I will update this review once my roof is either completed or my refund has been issued.

UPDATE: Andrey Tapia Espana, the owner, is refusing to refund my deductible & the 2 checks from the insurance company as I have chosen not to move forward with his company due to 4 reschedulings on his end, non-compliance with the state of MD, & recent reviews on different platforms posting very similar interactions. He informed me of receive my refund in the form of a cashier's check Saturday August 1st then stated August 2nd. I have received nothing. I even asked for photo proof that he actually has the cashier's check & I have received nothing. I have informed my insurance company and I will be filing multiple complaints & legal action.

UPDATE: 8/13/2026 THIS COMPANY HAS YET TO REFUND ME ANYTHING DESPITE TEXTING MY PHONE MULTIPLE TIMES STATING HE WOULD.

title: AG Heating Cooling Duct Cleaning

allreviews.name: Yufu Ma
allreviews.text:
I chose AG Heating Cooling Duct Cleaning in 2025 because their quote was cheaper than other companies. I paid approximately $7,900 for the installation of a new Trane HVAC system. Unfortunately, this turned out to be a very expensive mistake.

The Trane air conditioning system they installed had refrigerant leaks from the very beginning due to poor installation workmanship. The company promised a one-year warranty and service support, but they never came to inspect the system despite multiple requests.

Because we have another HVAC unit serving the attic and the outdoor temperatures were not extremely high for much of the year, we did not realize there was a problem until the summer of 2026, when the weather became much hotter. At that point, we discovered that the newly installed system had essentially lost all of its refrigerant and was barely providing any cooling.

After contacting AG again, they finally came out but charged additional fees for leak detection. Even after charging for diagnostics, they were unable to identify any leaks. Instead, they attempted to sell me an additional “leak sealant” service for approximately $395, which I declined.

I then hired another HVAC company. They were able to quickly locate two refrigerant leaks, both at the original brazed joints installed by AG. These leaks were found directly at the installation connections and strongly suggest poor workmanship during the original installation.

After I provided this information and evidence to AG, the company stopped responding entirely and ignored all further communications.

As a result of the prolonged refrigerant loss, I am now concerned that the compressor may also have suffered damage from operating under low refrigerant conditions.

I strongly recommend that homeowners carefully consider other HVAC contractors before hiring this company. A lower initial price is not worth poor workmanship, lack of warranty support, unnecessary additional charges, and being abandoned when serious installation problems are discovered.

Extremely disappointed with the installation quality, customer service, and accountability.

I have photos, videos, and leak test results confirming that the leaks originated from the original installation joints.

Please think carefully before trusting this company with a major HVAC installation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This response does not address the actual facts.

I requested an inspection only two months after installation because I was concerned the system was not operating properly. The company refused to come out. Less than one year after installation, the system had lost essentially all of its refrigerant.

After AG charged me $220 for leak detection and failed to locate the leaks, another licensed HVAC company found two leaks at the original brazed joints installed by AG. These were installation-related leaks, not “third-party errors.”

No third party had worked on or altered those joints before the leaks were discovered.

The company later offered to refund the $220 leak-detection fee if I deleted my review. I refused.

Instead of accusing the customer of intimidation, the company should explain why a newly installed system lost its refrigerant, why it refused to inspect the system when first contacted, and why another company was able to quickly find two leaks at AG’s original brazed connections.
